newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Germany seeks higher floor for EMU pact pleas.
newsitem.headline: Germany seeks higher floor for EMU pact pleas.

text.p: Germany is seeking to amend the draft text of a compromise deal on a pact to enforce fiscal discipline after the EU's planned monetary union (EMU), a senior German diplomat said.

He said Germany wanted to raise the floor proposed in the draft for enabling a country running a big fiscal deficit to claim exemption from fines on the grounds its economy was shrinking. The draft suggests shrinkage of 0.75 percent as the minimum for making such a plea.
"We would like to have 1.0 percent instead of 0.75 percent. Now there's still going to be some talking," the diplomat said.

"We have accepted 1.5 percent (shrinkage as an upper limit for allowing exemptions)," he said. Earlier Germany had demanded that the pact only allow automatic exemptions from fines if a country's GDP had shrunk 2.0 percent in a year.
Asked if this concession would be hard to sell back home, he said, "There will be a lot of criticism. This is our sacrifice on the German altar.... This is an Irish compromise."
He said the only argument was about the numbers in the draft text. "Everything else is settled."
